basis: Root comparison of unchanged teaching rule with existing exact-form word profiles. No new corpus count, native query, phonemic decoding or language selection.

No vowel grapheme is possible under the unchanged967literal-shape rule.
A joined ii could be a vowel grapheme; the profile does not establish that physical joining or its sound.

logic: 967uses bare e/i as consonants and only joined e/i runs of length2..7 as vowels. Therefore chedy and qokedy cannot contain a written vowel under its literal body binding, independent of any permutation of the consonant-key values. The rule must supply vowel-free spoken words at their actual broad recurrent use, not dismiss them as rare mistakes.
limits: No native sound or meaning is assigned.
This is not a universal claim that spoken languages prohibit consonant-only words; a later fixed source must actually support them.
Three readers are alternate transcriptions of one manuscript, not independent replications.
daiin is a contrasting possible vowel-bearing shape, not a confirmed phonemic reading.
No new aggregate vowel-free percentage or significance test is claimed.

decision: Do not prioritize further same-byte gap checks or build a decoder for967. Require a justified complete source/phonemic and physical contract with a different mandatory observable consequence before a full test. Raw construction and narrow positives stay recorded; missing support is not universal refutation.
